question: Give me a comprehensive list of all NBA basketball teams that went to the Finals and lost, including teams that won in other years.

message.content:
Based on the provided search results, a comprehensive list of all NBA teams that have gone to the Finals and lost, including teams that won championships in other years, cannot be fully compiled.

The results contain partial information about teams that have lost NBA Finals and some that have never lost, but they do not provide a complete, comprehensive list of every team that has ever appeared in the Finals and lost, regardless of their overall championship record.

However, the following information from the results is relevant:

*   The Los Angeles Lakers have lost the most NBA Finals in history, with 15 losses [3].
*   The Boston Celtics have won the most championships (18 as of 2024), and they have also lost Finals appearances [2].
*   The Chicago Bulls, Toronto Raptors, Baltimore Bullets, and Rochester Royals are listed as teams that have never lost in the NBA Finals [1].
*   The 10 teams that have never won an NBA championship (as of 2026) are the Brooklyn Nets, Orlando Magic, Indiana Pacers, Memphis Grizzlies, Minnesota Timberwolves, New Orleans Pelicans, San Antonio Spurs, Charlotte Hornets, Detroit Pistons, and Atlanta Hawks [2][5]. This list includes teams that have lost in the Finals and teams that have never reached the Finals.
*   The Brooklyn Nets have lost in the Finals in 2002 and 2003 [2].
*   The Indiana Pacers have lost in the Finals in 2000 and 2025 [5].
*   The Los Angeles Lakers have been in 32 NBA Finals and have won 17 times, meaning they have lost 15 times [3].
*   The results also list specific instances where both teams in the Finals were making their first appearance, such as the 2006 Miami Heat vs. Dallas Mavericks [4].

While these snippets provide details about some teams' Finals histories, they do not offer a complete list of all teams that have ever appeared in the Finals and lost.

# Which teams have never lost in the NBA Finals?

To remain undefeated at the biggest stage of the championship throughout franchise history has been a feat achieved by only a few NBA teams.

Teams that have never lost the NBA Finals (Image: FS)

The NBA Finals have been the ultimate decider of the championship crown since the first NBA Finals in 1947. A total of 77 teams have lifted the title till date. Decided in a best of seven games format, the final series is the last showdown between Conference champions on their way to title Glory. But how many teams have not lost in the NBA Finals in the history of the league?

To return with the title every time from an NBA Final is no petty feat. To remain undefeated at the biggest stage of the championship throughout franchise history, has been achieved by very few NBA teams.

passages.heading: Which teams have never lost in the NBA Finals?
passages.text:
Michael Jordan’s stellar record of six championships in six finals is one of his many legendary accomplishments. But to have done so as Finals MVP is another incredible feat entirely. That, however, is Jordan’s record across his 15 seasons in the NBA. But in a franchise’s history, through the ups and downs, it is near impossible to maintain a 100% Finals-win record – and very, very few teams have managed to do so. So, who are the teams that have never lost in the NBA Finals?

**Also Read**: Which teams have lost the most NBA Finals?

## Which teams have never lost in the NBA Finals?

Only four teams have recorded a hundred percent win percentage in the NBA Finals to date. The list includes the **Chicago Bulls, Toronto Raptors, Baltimore Bullets** and **Rochester Royals**.

passages.heading: Baltimore Bullets
passages.text:
## Baltimore Bullets

Back in the 1947-48 NBA Finals, it was the Baltimore Bullets who made it to one of the first finals hosted by the league.

They faced the Philadelphia Warriors in a six-game series, winning 4-2 to lift one of the first NBA titles in league history. But needless to say, no other franchise has been successful in replicating the dominance of Michael Jordan’s Chicago Bulls when it comes to Finals win percentage.

sources.title: Which NBA teams have never won a championship?

passages.text:
The Boston Celtics and Los Angeles Lakers are in a constant battle for the most championships in NBA history. In 2024, the Celtics won their 18th NBA title, breaking a tie with the Lakers. While Boston and Los Angeles duke it out at the top, 10 active franchises are still striving for their first titles.

In 2023, the Denver Nuggets became the latest team to join the list of all-time NBA champions, defeating the Miami Heat in the Finals and winning the franchise's first title. In the 2025 NBA Finals, the Indiana Pacers lost to the Oklahoma City Thunder, as they sought their first championship.

Here's a look at the 10 NBA teams that remain in search of their first championship, along with their number of Finals appearances. Three of the 10 qualified for the 2026 Playoffs, but with the Spurs defeating the Timberwolves in Game 6 of the Western Conference Semifinals, all 10 were eliminated and look to 2027 for another chance.

**Brooklyn Nets** **(2)**

The Nets won two ABA championships with Julius Erving leading the way but have fallen short of winning an NBA title since selling Erving to the Philadelphia 76ers at the ABA-NBA merger in 1976. The then-New Jersey Nets, led by Jason Kidd and Kenyon Martin, came close with back-to-back Finals appearances in 2002 and 2003. The Nets ran into Shaquille O'Neal and the Lakers one year and Tim Duncan and the San Antonio Spurs in the other.

Another relatively young franchise, the Pelicans have only been in New Orleans since 2002. They've got no championships and no Finals appearances. The club made its first march to the Western Conference semifinals with Chris Paul in 2008 as the New Orleans Hornets. New Orleans struck gold in 2012, winning the draft lottery and selecting Anthony Davis with the No. 1 pick. But the Pelicans fumbled the Davis years, only to watch him leave and win a championship with the Lakers.

**Orlando Magic (2)**

passages.heading: List of NBA franchise postseason droughts
passages.text: This is a list of National Basketball Association (NBA) franchise post-season appearance droughts. This list includes the all-time and the active consecutive non-playoffs. Aside from the NBA playoff appearance droughts, this list also includes droughts of series wins, appearances in the NBA Finals and NBA championship wins. The oldest franchise to never win the championship is the Suns (54 seasons), while the Royals/Kings and the Hawks have even longer championship droughts (71 and 64 seasons, respectively). Five franchises have never been to the NBA Finals, tied with the National Hockey League for the highest number among the major North American sports.<sup>[1]</sup> The oldest such team is the Braves/Clippers franchise (52 seasons); the Kings and the Hawks have appearance droughts that are even longer (71 and 61 seasons, respectively). The longest a franchise has gone without appearing in the playoffs at all is 16 seasons: the Kings franchise from 2006 to 2023.

passages.heading: List of NBA champions
passages.text: The NBA Finals is the annual championship series for the National Basketball Association (NBA) held at the conclusion of its postseason. All NBA Finals have been played in a best-of-seven format, and are contested between the winners of the Eastern Conference and the Western Conference (prior to 1971 it was played between division playoff winners), except in 1950 when the Eastern Division champion faced the winner between the Western and Central Division champions. From 1946 through 1949, when the league was known as the Basketball Association of America (BAA), the playoffs were a three-stage tournament where the two semifinal winners played each other in the finals.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup><sup>[3]</sup> The winning team of the series receives the Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy, which has been awarded since 1977 (between 1947 and 1976 the winning team received the Walter A. Brown Trophy).<sup>[4]</sup>

passages.heading: Champions
passages.text:
## Champions

[edit]
The most recent champions are the New York Knicks, who won their first championship since 1973. The Boston Celtics have won the most championships of any team in the league at 18.<sup>[5]</sup> As of 2026<sup>[update]</sup>, the Eastern champions have a 42–38 advantage in NBA titles over the Western champions. The 1949–50 Minneapolis Lakers, who won the NBA Finals, are counted in the Eastern versus Western champions record as they played that sole season in the Central Division before returning to the Western Division.

- The first parentheses in the *Western champions* and*Eastern champions* columns indicate the teams' playoff seed. The second parentheses indicate the number of times that teams have appeared in an NBA Finals as well as each respective team's NBA Finals record to date.
